messages:
devon: Heads-up — after the CUDA/driver update rolled to staging this morning we see a 12–18% p99 token-latency regression on the seq<=512 path. Not across all models but consistent on Falcon-40B and our midweight t0 variants. runtime-bot: [alert] perf-regression: staging/h100-cluster — p99 tokens +15% vs baseline (2026-03-17T09:12Z) devon: Repro steps: 1) spin up a 4xH100 staging shard with driver 535.xx 2) run generation loadtest with seq dist biased to 256/384 3) tail latencies go up vs driver 533 baseline aj: Can you paste the perf traces? even a sampling flame or top kernels helps. maria: I grabbed a short perf trace and kernel pick log. Paste below — note the sudden shift from cu_attn_fused_v2 -> cu_attn_generic for several layers at seq 256. ```
[2026-03-17T09:10:21Z] model=falcon-40b shard=stg-04 request_id=abc123
kernel_choice: layer3 attn => cu_attn_generic
kernel_choice: layer7 attn => cu_attn_generic
kernel_choice: layer11 attn => cu_attn_fused_v1
cpu: nvprof sample: cu_attn_generic 42% | cu_attn_fused_v1 27% | memcpy 10%```
devon: Interesting — autotuner seems to have re-ranked kernels after driver exposes a different PTX path. Could be kernel perf delta or subtle correctness guard causing slower path. oliver: Any KV-cache-related anomalies? We saw some KV-cache eviction churn last week on staging that might interact with batching heuristics. maria: KV cache hitrates are stable, but I did notice batcher is grouping more short requests into larger batches because per-token latency sampling skewed. That increases average seq processed per batch which can change chosen kernel. aj: Hypothesis: driver change nudged heuristics -> batching larger effective seq -> autotuner chooses generic kernel optimized for longer seqs -> regressions for mid-seq. Quick experiment idea: force batch max_seq_threshold=512 down to 384 and re-run. devon: Agreed. Also try forcing kernel blacklist for cu_attn_generic on the 256 path to confirm causality. oliver: I can push a canary config to staging. Which knobs do you want changed exactly? aj: Two knobs: --batcher.max_seq_threshold=384 and --autotune.blacklist=cu_attn_generic:seq<=512 (or a kernel gating rule). That will isolate batching vs kernel selection effects. maria: I ran a quick canary locally with blacklist and saw p99 drop ~10% back toward baseline for a small probe. Not conclusive but encouraging. ```
Local run (10min): baseline p99 98ms -> post-blacklist p99 87ms
CPU/GPU traces: cu_attn_fused_v2 resurfaces as dominant kernel```
devon: Good. Let's proceed with larger staging run. oliver: I'll deploy canary config to 20% of staging shards and run the 2-hour perf harness. Targeting deployment in ~30m. sre-oncall: If this looks okay we should also prepare a rollback plan for prod: pin driver packages on dedicated nodes and add a runtime knob to force legacy kernel policy. We should document operator commands. maria: I'll open a short RFC/ops doc with exact commands and a playbook. aj: Also collect per-layer kernel choose histograms and KV cache stats during canary. If we can prove mis-selection we can add a targeted autotune patch instead of blocking the driver. devon: Timeline: run canary -> collect traces -> decide EITHER (A) push targeted autotune override patch -> staged rollout OR (B) pin driver on Dedicated and coordinate vendor rollback. oliver: Noting that vendor is pushing this driver widely; vendor rollback may take days, so prefer targeted runtime mitigation if safe. runtime-bot: [task] canary-deploy-created -> stg-canary-1919876543 by oliver at 2026-03-17T09:45Z maria: I'll include a sample command in the playbook: ```
# force kernel gating via runtime flag
redwood-runtime --set autotune.kernel_gate="cu_attn_generic:disabled:seq<=512" --apply-to=stg-canary
# revert
redwood-runtime --unset autotune.kernel_gate --apply-to=stg-canary
``` aj: I'll run perf harness once canary is live and post results. devon: Thanks. If we see kernel mis-rank confirmed, let's prioritize a lightweight autotune config change (no binary build) and monitor for quality regressions. Also create an alert rule for sudden kernel pick shifts post-deploy. oliver: noted, I'll add ephemeral dashboards for kernel_choice per-layer. sre-oncall: I'm on standby for infra ops. Ping me if rollback to driver pin is needed. devon: 👍 closing loop — target decision in 3 hours after canary. reactions: :eyes: :rocket:
